output.summary: A sedge native to Iceland, Macaronesia, Europe and western Asia as far as the Himalayas, and possibly Greenland. It has been introduced to eastern Canada, New Jersey and Tasmania.
An evergreen dwarf shrub native to southern Spain, woolly lavender has striking silver, woolly leaves and deep violet-purple flower spikes with a familiar lavender scent.
A flowering shrub or small tree found from the central Himalayas to northern Indo-China. It has pointed, ribbed leaves and clusters of fragrant, pale pink flowers in autumn and winter.

A shrub, or sometimes a tree, endemic to China, where it grows in southern and north-central regions and Manchuria. It has pink or milky-white flowers and almost circular leaves that taper to a point.

A Mexican succulent native to the Durango–Sinaloa border and Chihuahua in the Sierra Madre Occidental, Echeveria affinis also occasionally occurs in San Luis Potosí. It grows at high elevations in rocky, very dry places and is adapted to poor, mineral-rich soils.

Perennial flowering herb native to Western and Central Europe, including the British Isles. It has white flowers with five petals split about halfway, and long, narrow grey-green leaves on roughly four-angled stems.

Shrub or tree endemic to eastern Australia, including Lord Howe Island. It has thin bark, usually white flowers borne singly on short side shoots, and fruit that can remain on the plant for a few years.

A dense deciduous shrub native to most of Europe, except the extreme north. Its foliage has a strong apple-like fragrance, while its stems bear many hooked prickles and its pink flowers develop into red hips.

output.summary: Flowering plant native to southern Macaronesia, specifically the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Salvage Islands.
Flowering plant; the subspecies Bufonia macropetala subsp. willkommiana is native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering perennial bulbous plant native to northeastern, southern and southeastern Brazil, the striped Barbados lily generally bears two to four relatively small, bright red flowers, each with a green stripe extending halfway along its segments. It also produces numerous small bulbs that help it escape cultivation and become established in tropical areas.

A palm tree known from two distinct populations in the Khasia Hills of northeast India and central northern Nepal, with others reported in Assam, Sikkim, Burma and southern China. Its leaves split regularly about halfway, and its coffee-bean-shaped seeds grow above a bare rather than fibrous trunk.
An alga native to Europe and Northern America, Lemanea fluviatilis belongs to the family Lemaneaceae.
An annual climbing herb, Cuscuta monogyna has simple, broad leaves.
Flowering plant whose eriocarpa and muricata varieties are native to mainland Portugal.

A robust herbaceous perennial native to Europe and Asia, including China, Japan, Kazakhstan, the Koreas, Mongolia, Siberia, Russia and Turkmenistan. It has aromatic, dark-green, deeply toothed leaves and small golden-yellow flowers in dense, flat-topped clusters in summer.

output.summary: An annual flowering plant native to Europe, southwestern Asia, North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, Korea and Japan. It has a sprawling habit, usually bold blue flowers and dull green, toothed leaves; its hairy fruit capsule has two parallel lobes.
A flowering plant endemic to Madeira, Portugal, Sinapidendron gymnocalyx belongs to the mustard family.

Flowering plant almost endemic to the mountains of central and northern mainland Portugal. It grows above 1,000 metres in stony meadows and granite rock crevices and is assessed as Vulnerable, with only five known locations.

A perennial shrub native to the coasts of Southern California and Baja California, it grows low, sending long reddish stems horizontally. Its dark, glossy leaves have paler, leathery undersides and glands that release sticky, citrus-scented sap. Deep red flower clusters appear from late winter into early spring, followed by small red fruits later in spring.

A flowering perennial herb native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa, common hedge-nettle forms spreading patches in grassland, meadows and open woods. Its upright stems bear wrinkled, toothed leaves with heart-shaped bases, and it flowers from July to September.

A tropical and subtropical pioneer plant, it most likely originates from Central or South America, although its precise origin is unknown. Its narrow leaves are covered with stiff hairs, while its flower heads combine white outer florets with yellow central florets.
A flowering plant, its acuminata and aestiva subspecies are native to mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Crepis lampsanoides belongs to the daisy family.
A flowering grass whose subspecies Festuca brigantina subsp. brigantina is endemic to mainland Portugal. This subspecies is protected under Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin, it is found from Mexico and the West Indies to subtropical South America. It grows in habitats ranging from tropical savanna and forest to mountains, shrubland and grassland, and has not been documented north of Mexico.

A tiny duckweed native to parts of the Americas, though its exact native range is unknown, least duckweed is the smallest Lemna species. Its translucent green body grows singly in shade and usually in pairs in full sun, and it produces a short-lived flower.

An annual herb native to Europe and Western Asia, Mediterranean hartwort has softly hairy, divided leaves and white flowers with enlarged, deeply two-lobed petals. Its round, flattened fruit is elaborately textured. The leaves are eaten in Greece as a cooked green and salad vegetable, while in Italy the plant is used as a condiment.

output.summary: A thorny understorey shrub or small tree native to southeastern Queensland and northeastern New South Wales, Australia, the finger lime has aromatic leaves and cylindrical, slightly curved fruits. Its edible fruits contain tangy, pearl-like juice vesicles used fresh or in recipes; they are also made into marmalade and pickles, while dried peel is used as a spice.
output.edibilityNote: Fruits are eaten fresh or used in recipes, marmalade and pickles; dried peel is used as a spice.

output.summary: A flowering herb native to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa, Galium viscosum grows in fallow land and traditional rain-fed olive groves on basic soils. In mainland Portugal, it was assessed as Vulnerable in 2020, with small, widely scattered populations in the south.

A flowering plant native to North America, American searocket commonly grows on beaches and dunes. It is a short, succulent shrub with thick leaves that vary in their teeth and lobes. It is annual in northern latitudes but may survive as a biennial in warmer climates.

output.summary: Flowering plant native to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil.
A flowering plant in the mustard family, Sinapidendron frutescens has two listed subspecies, both endemic to Madeira.

Bearberry is a small evergreen groundcover shrub widely distributed across circumboreal regions of the subarctic Northern Hemisphere. It has shiny, thick leaves, clusters of white-to-pink flowers and bright red fruits that persist into early winter.

output.summary: Tropical evergreen shrub native to Peru. Its short-lived white flowers emerge one after another from overlapping bright yellow bracts throughout the warm months.
A moss with no stated native origin, urn hair moss is found across Europe, North America and parts of Asia. Its robust, upright growth may look bluish-green when moist, and its stems are wine red.

An evergreen shrub presumed native to temperate Andean regions of Colombia, Peru and Chile, pepino is not known in the wild. It bears sweet edible fruit with melon-like colour and a flavour resembling honeydew and cucumber, often eaten fresh as a snack.

output.summary: A bulbous perennial native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, silver squill is often cultivated and grows well with minimal care.
Flowering plant whose subspecies Nepeta tuberosa subsp. tuberosa is native to mainland Portugal. It belongs to the mint family.

A freshwater microscopic green alga with a cosmopolitan distribution, Pseudopediastrum boryanum occurs most commonly in nutrient-rich waters, but also in brackish water and some mountain water bodies. Its colonies form flat, star-like discs, while its decay-resistant cell walls are often preserved in lake sediments.

Herbaceous perennial tuberous plant native to the Mediterranean region, the poppy anemone bears single, showy flowers with black centres. Wild flowers are usually red but may be white or blue, blooming from winter to early spring in their native range.

An evergreen shrub endemic to Oregon and California in the United States, blueblossom has glossy green leaves and spring clusters of tiny flowers ranging from shades of blue to nearly white. It attracts birds, butterflies and other pollinators, while honeybees often visit for pollen.

A medium-sized deciduous tree native across Europe and temperate Asia and to northern Morocco, silver birch is mainly mountainous in the southern parts of its range. It has white, peeling bark and slender, often drooping twigs, while its roughly triangular leaves turn yellow in autumn.
output.edibilityNote: In spring, tapped sap may be drunk fresh, concentrated like maple syrup, or fermented into wine.

output.summary: A winter annual grass native to the Mediterranean, great brome has hairy, rough leaves and a broad, nodding seed head like an oat plant. Its very sharp seeds have backward-facing barbs that can catch and lodge like fish hooks, posing a danger to animals.
Rose native to central, southern and southeastern Europe, including southwestern Russia. Its fruit persists for about 30 days and contains about 23 seeds on average.

A deciduous flowering shrub native to dense forests from the Himalayas through southern China to Taiwan. It has coarse, broadly oval leaves and large, flat flower heads in late summer, typically pale blue or pink with white or pale pink florets around the edges.

Perennial herb native to central and southern Italy, including Sicily, purple toadflax has upright stems topped with clusters of flowers. Its flowers are usually dark purple or violet, rarely pale or white, and bloom from April to October.

An annual flowering plant native to Belgium, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, Spain and Switzerland. It has four prominently unequal petals; wild plants have white or pale violet flowers, while cultivated varieties may be deeper pink, violet or fuchsia.

A palm native to southern Brazil and Paraguay, it usually grows in small populations. Its solitary trunk is wrapped in persistent, criss-crossed fibres ending in woody spines, while its fan-shaped leaves are dark green above and silvery beneath.

A deciduous tree native to the midwestern United States, northern catalpa has an uncertain original range. It has large, heart-shaped leaves and white, trumpet-shaped flowers marked with yellow stripes and purple spots. Its long, thin brown fruit capsules often remain on the tree through winter.

Perennial herb native to North America, the Great Plains flatsedge grows in sunny, open places such as prairies, fields and roadsides. It spreads through underground stems and has triangular stalks topped by densely clustered, roughly spherical spikes.
